purpose: Closed vocabulary for synthetic Qwen3-TTS blueprints. Acoustic identity and textual speech style are separately classified; every value is closed, evidenced, and rendered deterministically.

models.rule: VoiceDesign only produces reference clips. Dialogue lines are always generated by the Base model with a cached ICL prompt. Mood never reaches the Base model as text.

reference.text: Good evening. The road ahead is quiet tonight, although the weather may change before morning. Keep to the marked path, and listen for the bells. Have you brought everything you need?
rules: Every character and every mood uses this exact text. A shared script makes voices comparable and keeps ICL extraction uniform.
Do not translate, trim, or personalize the script per character.
Reject a recording shorter than 8 s or longer than 18 s; regenerate with the same seed offset instead of editing the audio.
Store the exact transcript with every generated clip; ICL requires ref_text to match the audio word for word.
The open-weight model has a reported ICL startup artifact where the first words of the reference leak into the output. Check the first 2 s of a new profile before approving it.

presentation.question: How is the voice heard, not what the character's body or gender identity is?

masculine.notes: A deliberate synthetic vocal presentation; game sex metadata may inform a creative choice but is never acoustic evidence.

feminine.notes: A deliberate synthetic vocal presentation; game sex metadata may inform a creative choice but is never acoustic evidence.

androgynous.notes: Deliberately ambiguous presentation; choose only as a marked synthetic casting decision or when a source explicitly describes it.

neutral.notes: Minimal gender cue. Useful for narrators, generic voices, and characters whose vocal presentation is unstated.

nonhuman.notes: Beast, lifeless, or ethereal timbre. Experimental: Qwen3-TTS is a speech model and may render this as an odd human voice. Always audition.

synthetic.notes: Mammets, nodes, Allagan constructs. Experimental, audition required.

perceived_age.question: How old does the voice sound, not how old the character is in lore years?
notes: Use perceived vocal age. A 100-year-old Elezen may sound like a young adult; a 30-year-old Lalafell still sounds adult, never childlike.
Null is allowed and preferred over a guess. The renderer simply omits the age clause.
Never combine an age with a presentation that contradicts it (child + mature); one value only by construction.
Register describes where the voice sits, not how expressive it is.
Body size and race are not sufficient evidence for a register; they are at most creative_selection.
Extreme ends (very_low, very_high) require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Optional. Omit when unsure; the model defaults to a natural range.

timbre_primary.question: What is the dominant texture of the voice?
notes: This is the single most differentiating field after pitch. Spend the creative effort here.
Values that share a family are acoustically redundant; the validator rejects combining two of them (husky + gravelly is one instruction, not two).
At most one secondary texture, from a different family than the primary.
Two overlapping roughness words muddle the instruction; three guarantee mush.
Preferred secondary use is a light modifier: slightly breathy, slightly nasal, a hint of reediness.
Optional. Omit rather than guess; a wrong resonance clause is a bigger error than a missing one.
How consonants and vowels are formed. Default for ordinary NPCs is relaxed or crisp.
slurred, drawling, staccato, and sharp are acting choices and require explicit or supported_inference evidence.
Pace is a rhythm property of the voice, not an emotion. An angry character is not automatically fast.
measured and moderate cover most NPCs; very_slow and very_fast need evidence.
Default natural. Prefer natural or restrained; dramatic and melodic make a character's every line theatrical.
Personality traits such as stoic or arrogant may justify restrained, but only as supported_inference.
Profile and strength are set together or both omitted; the validator rejects half an accent.
Qwen3-TTS has no accent mode. Accent clauses are soft hints; verify by listening before approving a profile.
Never derive an accent from a nation or race alone. Use the project default when the wiki says nothing.
The project default is evidence level 'default', never 'explicit'.
Embellishments, never mandatory. Omit most of the time.
A trait whose family matches an already selected timbre, resonance, or articulation is redundant and is rejected.

moods.status: generated per character and auditioned; not per-line
moods.purpose: The mood layer is a separate reference recording per state. It exists so the same identity can be performed in different emotional registers without redrawing the character.
implementation_rules: A mood is baked into its own VoiceDesign reference clip and its own cached ICL prompt. It is never passed to the Base model as text.
The identity prompt is identical across a character's archons; only the trailing mood block differs.
Every archon speaks the same reference script as the neutral clip.
NEVER select an archon per dialogue line. Listening on 2026-11-01 found the shift between archons far too large: the same character would change voice mid-conversation.
Archon choice is a casting decision made once per character, recorded in pack_archon, and defaulting to neutral.
Neutral is the basis. It is deliberately the least expressive of the archons and is what every character packs with until a source justifies otherwise.
Add an archon only when the source material describes how the character sounds by default, not when a scene happens to be emotional.
Every character needs a neutral archon. Mood archons are optional and are auditioned against each other before one is chosen for packing.

neutral.classification_description: No distinct default register: ordinary, unforced delivery. Choose this only when the character genuinely reads as neutral; choose none when the evidence is too thin to tell the difference.

calm.classification_description: Habitually settled and unhurried, with steady volume even when the scene is tense.

happy.classification_description: Habitually warm and upbeat; the good humour is part of the character, not one reaction.

sad.classification_description: Habitually subdued and low-energy; a persistent melancholy in ordinary talk.

angry.classification_description: Habitually forceful and clipped; irritation or command is the baseline, not an outburst.

fearful.classification_description: Habitually nervous and rushed; anxiety shows in ordinary lines, not only in danger.

secretive.classification_description: Habitually hushed and conspiratorial; speaks as if someone may be listening.

rules: The neutral variant is the identity prompt alone. It exists as a preset only so a profile can override it; with no overrides the renderer emits no mood block and the identity text is used verbatim.
Presets are the only moods. Do not invent free-form mood names.
Overrides may change at most two fields from the preset; a third override means the preset is wrong and should be corrected here first.
Reserve extreme intensity for a deliberate decision; ordinary dialogue lives at subtle to moderate.
shouting and whispering are production styles, not emotions; do not use them as the default mood of a character.
moods.definition: One mood reference is an ARCHON: a designed reference clip plus its cached ICL prompt. A character owns a small set of archons (neutral plus whichever moods the source justifies). A pack uses exactly one archon for all of that character's lines, and that archon's clip is pinned by hash.

archon_pinning.unit: the reference clip, not a per-line seed
archon_pinning.rule: One approved reference WAV per archon is stored and hashed. Every dialogue line for that character is cloned from that clip through create_voice_clone_prompt, so identity is fixed without seeding individual lines.
archon_pinning.why_not_a_line_seed: Measured 2026-11-01: two lines from the same take score 0.991-0.994 cosine, two lines from different takes 0.984-0.994, and per-line pitch scatter inside one take exceeds the mean gap between takes. A line seed does not carry identity.
archon_pinning.why_not_only_a_design_seed: The same seed produces a different clip when dtype, attention backend, torch build, or the reference script change. The hash is the durable guarantee; the design seed is kept for reproducibility.

archon_none.classification_description: Not enough evidence for any default emotional register. Packs the neutral archon.

render.identity_template: {article} {age}{presentation} voice{pitch}{pitch_range}. It has a {timbre}{timbre_secondary}{resonance}. Speech is {articulation} with {intonation} intonation, at a {pace} pace{accent}.{traits} Neutral conversational delivery for game dialogue.
render.mood_template: For this take, speak with {phrase}, at {intensity} emotional intensity. Use {energy} vocal energy, {projection} projection, and a {pace} speaking pace. The delivery should carry {pitch_movement} intonation, {articulation} articulation, and {rhythm} rhythm.
render.mood_composition: mood_instruct = identity_prompt + ' ' + mood_template(rendered). The identity text is byte-identical across every mood of a character; only the trailing mood block changes.
render.article_rule: Use 'An' when the rendered phrase starts with a vowel sound (adult, ageless, ancient, elderly, androgynous), otherwise 'A'.
render.banned_identity_words_reason: Identity is the constant; emotion belongs to the mood layer. An emotion word in the identity prompt makes every line of the character permanently emotional.
render.word_target_note: 48 is the hard ceiling: it still fits accent plus secondary timbre plus two traits. Anything longer dilutes the description, and Qwen's own voice-design examples are shorter.
render.style_template: The wording is {register} in register, {vocabulary_complexity} in vocabulary, {sentence_complexity} in sentence structure, {colloquialism} in colloquialism, and {rhetorical_style} in rhetorical shape.
render.style_note: Optional speech-style clause rendered only when a plan asks for it; it describes wording, never pitch, timbre, or accent.

values.explicit: A source directly describes this audible quality or factual field; retain its exact supporting quote and provenance.
values.supported_inference: Multiple attributed source statements support this value; retain the relevant source quotes and provenance.
values.creative_selection: A deliberate synthetic casting decision, not a claim about an original recording or actor.
values.default: A named project fallback from this vocabulary; not source evidence.
values.unknown: Insufficient reliable information; optional fields remain null.

rules: Every non-null acoustic identity field has one evidence record.
explicit and supported_inference require source URL or game-data identifier, source type, and exact short quote.
creative_selection and default are clearly labelled and must not impersonate source facts.
unknown is valid only for nullable fields.
Race, clan, sex, body, occupation, and personality cannot be acoustic evidence.

allowed: An explicit source description of audible qualities can support the matching closed acoustic field.
Dialogue measurements can support speech-style classification only; they do not establish pitch, timbre, resonance, articulation, or accent.
Race, clan, sex, body, age appearance, occupation, and personality may be considered only as creative context and must be labeled creative_selection, never as acoustic fact.
A stated lore age may be recorded as lore metadata; do not convert species lifespan to perceived vocal age.
forbidden: Race, clan, sex, height, build, or body mass as evidence for pitch, timbre, resonance, articulation, pace, or accent.
Occupation as evidence for timbre or pitch (a craft role does not make a voice gravelly).
Personality as evidence for pitch, timbre, resonance, age, or accent (cheerfulness does not mean high pitch).
Dialogue-derived vocabulary complexity or sentence length as evidence of articulation, accent, pitch, or timbre.
Mood words as permanent identity fields.
Adding emotion to the identity prompt because a character is usually emotional.
Inventing lore facts, acoustic evidence, or source quotations.
inference_policy.required_for_allowed_inferences: Every audible selection without an exact source quote is creative_selection or default. Creative casting is not a claim about an original actor.

profile_rules: One canonical profile per NPC id. Labels that resolve to the same NPC share the profile.
Unnamed or generic labels get a bank archetype profile, not a new invented voice.
A character profile never stores audio, seeds, or paths; reference recordings and cached prompts live in the generated voice directory.
profiles are versioned; bump profile_version whenever a selected value changes, so already-generated lines can be traced to the voice that produced them.

checks: reference_duration_ok: the neutral clip is 10-15 s.
reference_transcript_verified: the stored transcript matches the audio word for word.
no_reference_leak: the first 2 s of a held-out clone do not repeat the reference tail.
identity_approved: a human listened and accepted the voice as the character.
no_drift: two independent clone lines are recognisably the same speaker.

speech_style.purpose: Closed classification of how text is written and phrased. Speech style is separate from acoustic identity and is never appended to the VoiceDesign identity prompt.

register.question: What register best describes the dialogue wording?

formal.classification_description: Uses consistently formal constructions and formal signal words.

neutral.classification_description: Neither strongly formal nor strongly colloquial.

conversational.classification_description: Uses casual constructions, colloquial terms, or frequent contractions.

vocabulary_complexity.question: How complex is the character’s vocabulary, based on the sampled text?

plain.classification_description: Mostly common, short words and direct phrasing.

ordinary.classification_description: Everyday vocabulary with a typical range.

educated.classification_description: Frequent longer or less common vocabulary.

poetic.classification_description: Unusually figurative, image-rich, or lyrical word choice.

sentence_complexity.question: How structurally complex are the sampled utterances?

simple.classification_description: Mostly short utterances with few subordinate clauses.

mixed.classification_description: A mixture of short and multi-clause utterances.

complex.classification_description: Frequently long utterances or multiple subordinate clauses.

colloquialism.question: How often does the dialogue use colloquial wording?

low.classification_description: Rare colloquial signal words and informal constructions.

moderate.classification_description: Some colloquial wording mixed with neutral phrasing.

high.classification_description: Frequent colloquial words, contractions, or informal constructions.

diction_style.question: Which wording style best fits the dialogue?

plain.classification_description: Direct word choice without ornate phrasing.

rhetorical_style.question: What rhetorical pattern is most representative of the dialogue?

direct.classification_description: Short, plain statements that get to the point.

flowing.classification_description: Long linked clauses and continuous phrasing.

fragmented.classification_description: Many short fragments or interrupted phrases.

inquisitive.classification_description: Questions form a prominent recurring pattern.

emphatic.classification_description: Exclamations or marked emphasis recur in the wording.

contraction_frequency.question: How frequently does the dialogue use contractions?

low.classification_description: Contractions are rare in the sample.

speech_habits.question: Which repeated textual speech habits occur in the sample?

signals.dialect_note: Dialect and archaic address forms. They weight which lines are sampled and are counted for the model, but they are deliberately NOT part of the formal/colloquial rate: 'ye' and 'pray' are archaic, not informal, and folding them into the register measurement would corrupt it.

speech_style.measurement_rules: All counters and rates are calculated from distinct voice_line_id samples. The interpretation is a deterministic rule mapping; retain measurements separately from interpretation.

classification.provider_contract: RulesProvider works offline. JevProvider sends one structured System One request for independent decisions. Jev output selects from this vocabulary and never provides factual source citations.

identity_resolved.instructions: Is this dossier safely tied to one canonical FFXIV NPC identity with no known SE voice reference?

criteria.true: One resolved NPC identity and no voiced alias.
criteria.false: Identity is ambiguous, unresolved, or has an SE voice reference.

individual_design.instructions: How strongly does the evidence justify a unique individual synthetic voice design instead of a shared archetype?
levels: Generic or unresolved identity with too little evidence for a unique design.
Minor identity with sparse or repetitive dialogue and no distinctive source evidence.
Some distinctiveness, but a shared archetype remains a reasonable fit.
Distinctive character or rich dialogue supports an individual creative cast.
Strong, explicit voice description and substantial character-specific evidence justify an individual design.

voice_evidence_present.instructions: Does the dossier contain a source quote that explicitly describes an audible voice quality?

criteria.true: At least one attributed source quote describes an audible quality.
criteria.false: No source quote describes an audible voice quality.

mood.preset.instructions: Which single mood preset describes how this character sounds by DEFAULT across ordinary dialogue? Judge the baseline register across unrelated lines, never the strongest scene. Use only the dialogue lines in this state; lore or personality text is not mood evidence. Choose none when the lines do not show one consistent register, when they are mostly quest instructions, or when the volume is too small to tell; none is the correct answer far more often than not.

mood.justified.instructions: Does the dialogue itself show a default emotional register for this character, rather than the emotion of individual scenes?

criteria.true: Lines from unrelated scenes share one register, and ordinary lines carry it as clearly as dramatic ones.
criteria.false: The register varies by scene, the lines are mostly instructions or one-off exclamations, or there are too few lines to tell.

speech_style.register.instructions: Which register best describes the actual wording in the sampled dialogue?

speech_style.vocabulary_complexity.instructions: How complex is the vocabulary in the sampled dialogue? Judge words, not the character’s intelligence or social class.

speech_style.sentence_complexity.instructions: How structurally complex are the sampled utterances? Judge the text only.

speech_style.colloquialism.instructions: How often does the sampled dialogue use colloquial wording?

speech_style.rhetorical_style.instructions: What rhetorical pattern is most representative of the sampled dialogue?

confidence_policy: Choice confidence and probability are both retained; low confidence routes to review or a shared archetype.
Noul returns a yes probability, not a separate confidence field; interpret it with the configured yes/no thresholds.
A Score carries its distribution, expected score, and confidence. A high signal is not proof of correctness.
Thresholds are initial project settings and must be calibrated against manually reviewed examples.

A mood preset is decided from dialogue alone: the dossier must clear min_dialogue_lines_for_mood, the dialogue pool is split into chunk windows, and every window is asked the same typed questions. The preset is accepted only when the mean distribution clears mood_probability, the same preset leads at least mood_consistency_ratio of the chunks, the mean distribution stays under mood_dispersion_limit, and the mean none+neutral mass stays under mood_abstention_mass. There is no separate confidence gate: on this model confidence is a linear rescaling of the top probability, so a second threshold would only re-ask the probability question. mood.justified is recorded as advisory evidence and never blocks. Otherwise the pack archon is neutral and mood.blocked_by names every failed gate.
Speech-style choices below min_dialogue_lines_for_style are recorded as insufficient rather than answered; the profile then carries no style and renders from identity alone.
classification.acoustic_family_compatibility: Primary and optional secondary timbres must use different acoustic families. Distinctive traits cannot repeat the selected primary family.
classification.speech_style_separation: Speech-style results stay out of the identity prompt and never become acoustic evidence.

profile_lifecycle.approval_rule: Only a human review action may set approved. Classification confidence and human approval are separate fields.

schema_migrations.1.0_to_1.1: Adds speech-style classifications, lifecycle and classification provenance. Existing identity selections and the Qwen reference script keep their original meanings. Use the explicit blueprint migration command; old profiles are never silently rewritten.
schema_migrations.reference_script_policy: The schema 1.0 npc_reference_v1 script remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
